title: Shipping UniPucks to a synchrotron in a dry shipper
summary: Pack up to 16 pins per UniPuck, stack pucks in a dry-shipper dewar charged with liquid nitrogen, and send by courier to the beamline. The UniPuck is the standard that European synchrotron sample changers accept.

steps.text: Load up to 16 pins per UniPuck, crystals upward, under LN2.
Place pucks in the shipping cane/canister; a CX100-type dewar takes up to 7 pucks (112 samples), newer high-throughput dewars up to 24 (384).
Charge the dry-shipper dewar with LN2 until the absorbent liner is saturated, let it settle, then pour off free liquid.

duration_s.note: Standard dry-shipper conditioning is hours; source gives no time. 2 h assumed.

steps.text: Insert the cane and close the shipper; keep it upright and avoid tipping.
Register the shipment with the facility and send by courier, checking that cold holding time covers transit plus delays.
At the facility the pucks are loaded on the beamline sample changer (e.g. Diamond I04-1).

safety: Liquid nitrogen: eye and hand protection; ventilate rooms.
Dry shippers must be stood upright; do not ship damaged ones.
Check courier dangerous-goods rules for nitrogen dry shippers.

source.publisher: Acta Crystallographica Section D (IUCr, via PMC)

notes: Diamond's own shipping pages (dry shipping puck holders) were found in search results but returned 403 when opened, so facility-specific rules are NOT paraphrased here; consult them. Pflugrath 2015 (PMC4461322) adds: fill dry shippers with LN2 on arrival, dry the foam after use, use overnight couriers.
